senses.gloss:
Pāman occurs in the Atharvaveda^1 as the name of a skin
disease. The derivative adjective, Pāmana, ‘suffering from
skin disease,’ is found in the later Saṃhitās and the Brāhmaṇas.^2
Since it is mentioned as an accompaniment of fever, probably
a cutaneous eruption or scab consequent on fever is meant.
1) v. 22, 12. Cf. for the reading,
Whitney, Translation of the Atharva-
veda, 261. See also Chāndogya Upani-
ṣad, iv. 1, 8.
2) Taittirīya Saṃhitā, vi. 1, 3, 8;
Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā, xxiii. 4; Śatapatha
Brāhmaṇa, iii. 2, 1, 31.
Cf. Grohmann, Indische Studien, 9,
401 et seq.; Zimmer, Altindisches Leben,
388; Schrader, Prehistoric Antiquities,
421, n.; Bloomfield, Hymns of the
Atharvaveda, 450, 451; Atharvaveda,
63.
